newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sells 2.5 bln dong T-bills, rate 8.20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sells 2.5 bln dong T-bills, rate 8.20 pct.

text.p: Vietnam sold 2.5 billion dong ($225,510) worth of six-month Treasury bills to domestic institutions at an auction on Wednesday, an official at the State Bank of Vietnam said.
The annual coupon of the bills was 8.20 percent.
At the last auction of government paper on November 20, the central bank issued 2.9 billion dong worth of one-year notes at a rate of 8.00 percent.
The Bank had originally said 50 billion dong worth of six-month bills were on offer at the auction.

Bids for Treasury stock had been coming in far higher than the Ministry of Finance was prepared to accept at recent sales. As a result, much less stock had been allocated at each sale than the central bank originally offered.
The maturity date of the bills sold on Wednesday is May 27, 1997.
The bank said allotments of stock, in dong, were as follows:
Bank for Investment and Development of Vietnam 2.0 billion
